## C2 — Confusables and KG hints, Licensing, permits and the driving tests

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A01
The sixty day window to get a Vermont license after moving in applies to a regular license, while a commercial license from another state must be transferred within the shorter window of thirty days [A01].
Why it matters: group residency clocks; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F01, sec01-F02
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A02
The one year a learner's permit must be held before a junior license is a different clock from the six month clean record period, which counts only the six months immediately before applying [A02].
Why it matters: group junior license eligibility; difficulty medium; prereq sec01-F11; confusables sec01-F11, sec01-F08
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A03
The forty hours of certified practice driving are counted separately from the six behind the wheel hours of the driver education course, so the two never overlap [A03].
Why it matters: group driver education hours; difficulty medium; prereq sec01-F13, sec01-F14; confusables sec01-F17, sec01-F13
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A04
The junior license passenger rules move in three steps: driving alone for the first three months, family members during the second three months, and no passenger limit after six months, with the safety belt count capping every step [A04].
Why it matters: group junior license restrictions; difficulty high; prereq sec01-F12; confusables sec01-F26, sec01-F27
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A07
A failed road test brings a one week wait, but a third failure raises the wait to at least one month, and neither matches the one day wait after a failed knowledge test [A07].
Why it matters: group test retake waits; difficulty medium; prereq sec01-F41; confusables sec01-F44, sec01-F41
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A05
A new resident whose out-of-state license is valid or expired three years or less needs only an eye examination, while one expired more than three years must take the vision, written and road tests like a first-time applicant [A05].
Why it matters: group license transfer; difficulty medium; prereq sec01-F31; confusables sec01-F31, sec01-F15
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A06
A Type Two school bus endorsement on a regular license covers buses rated for fewer than sixteen passengers, while sixteen or more passengers or a heavy weight rating moves the driver into commercial licensing with passenger and school bus endorsements [A06].
Why it matters: group endorsements; difficulty medium; prereq sec01-F33; confusables sec01-F33, sec01-F50
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0018]
